news.title: Capital Football duo set to represent Australia at IFCPF World Cups in Atlanta
news.lede: Two products of Capital Football’s All Abilities program will fly the flag for the ACT this October, with Luc Launder and Carly Salmon named in the CommBank Pararoos and CommBank ParaMatildas squads for the IFCPF World Cups in Atlanta, USA. Launder, a defender, has been selected in the 14-player CommBank Pararoos squad for the IFCPF Men’s World Cup 2026, running from 12 to 24 October. Head Coach Kai Lammert’s side has been drawn into Group B alongside Brazil, Spain and Chile, with all matches to be played at the U.S. Soccer National Training Center.

news.title: Here we come! Young Ferns qualify for 2027 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have qualified for next year’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after beating Papua New Guinea 3-0 in Honiara. The win, in the semi-finals of the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship, ensures New Zealand will be one of Oceania’s two representatives at the 2027 global tournament. It will be New Zealand’s 11th consecutive appearance at the U-16 World Cup. The second qualifying spot at the World Cup will go to New Caledonia who beat Fiji 1-0 in the other semi-final.

news.title: Beckham backs Messi for Ballon d'Or after 100th Miami goal
news.lede: Messi joined Inter Miami in the summer of 2023. Lionel Messi deserves to win this year's Ballon d'Or, according to Inter Miami co-owner and former England captain David Beckham. The 39-year-old Argentina great, who has won the global player of the year award eight times and has been nominated on the 30-player shortlist for 2026, scored his 100th goal for Miami on Wednesday. He also provided an assist for Casemiro to score their second goal in a 2-0 victory over Cruz Azul that clinched the Campeones Cup - an annual match contested by US and Mexican cup winners.

news.title: FIFA rebuffs Morocco claim over 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: FIFA said on Friday that a decision on the venue for the 2030 World Cup final would be made "in due course", after Moroccan football federation president Fouzi Lekjaa said the showpiece match would be staged in Morocco. Morocco, Spain and Portugal are co-hosting the 2030 tournament and have already begun competing for the right to stage the final, with Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu and a planned 115,000-seat stadium in Benslimane, near Casablanca, viewed as the leading contenders. Lekjaa said on Wednesday that the final would take place in Morocco. "Benslimane province will host the World Cup final.

news.title: 2014 World Cup star James Rodriguez retires from national team
news.lede: Colombian football star James Rodriguez, one of the best players in the country's history, on Tuesday announced his retirement from the national team after 15 years and three World Cups. "I'm leaving with serenity because I know I gave absolutely everything," the 35-year-old captain said in a social media video, his eyes welling with tears. Rodriguez powered himself and his country to stardom at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, when Los Cafeteros made the quarterfinals for the first time. He won the tournament's Golden Boot as the top scorer and became a global superstar.

news.title: World Cup Final should be at Barcelona’s Camp Nou, says Joan Laporta
news.lede: “It shouldn’t be Casablanca or Madrid; it should be the Spotify Camp Nou.” That’s how FC Barcelona’s president, Joan Laporta, put it, in an interview with Spanish radio. He wants the FIFA World Cup final to be played at Barcelona’s refurbished home, urging football’s governing body to pass over Madrid, Spain’s capital, and Casablanca, Morocco’s largest city. He jokingly dismissed those rival bids, saying “Casablanca and Madrid are the same thing.”

news.title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing
news.lede: Coach says Argentina’s gung-ho approach forced hand. ‘No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more’. Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina this summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early. Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour.
